Formula 1 heads to Mexico City this weekend for round 19 of 23, with the Mexico City Grand Prix set for Sunday, November 1, at 2 p.m. Mexico City time (3 p.m. ET) at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez. Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli leads the drivers' championship with 365 points, 123 ahead of teammate George Russell and 124 ahead of Lewis Hamilton, after winning the United States Grand Prix on October 25 for his ninth victory of the season.

The clinching math is simple: Antonelli is champion on Sunday if he finishes ninth or better, or if neither Russell nor Hamilton wins the race. At 20 years and 68 days, he would become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history, beating Sebastian Vettel's 2010 record. Max Verstappen, who has won five times at this circuit, is mathematically out of the title fight, while Mercedes, leading Ferrari by 133 points, can also settle the constructors' championship in Mexico, the earliest round it can be decided.

Verstappen remains a threat for the race win itself after ending a two-race winning streak in Austin, where Antonelli won from pole. Last year's Mexico City race was won by Lando Norris for McLaren, ahead of Charles Leclerc and Verstappen, and Carlos Sainz won here for Ferrari in 2024. The 71-lap race at altitude, with its long main straight, has long rewarded both straight-line speed and clean starts into the first corner.

Qualifying is set for Saturday afternoon, with practice sessions opening the weekend on Friday. A dry, warm weekend is forecast for qualifying and race day in Mexico City.

Sources: TSN; Covers; TheSpread.com; Hollywoodbets Sports Blog.

title: F1 Mexico City Grand Prix Preview: Antonelli Can Clinch the Title on Sunday at Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
